content: A nursing school is an educational institution designed to provide the necessary education and training for individuals to become fully qualified nurses. The structure and requirements of nursing education vary significantly across different countries. United Kingdom Florence Nightingale was instrumental in establishing the concept of formal nursing education. In 1860, she founded the Nightingale Training School for Nurses at St. Thomas' Hospital in London. Her primary goal was to train nurses to a professional standard, emphasizing the development of observational skills and sensitivity to patient needs. Graduates of her program were then able to work in hospitals across the UK and internationally. Nursing education in the UK has since evolved and is now offered at numerous universities. The University of Manchester was among the first institutions in England to provide nursing education at the degree level. Admission requirements for nursing programs typically include five GCSEs (or Standard Grades), including English, mathematics, and a science subject (preferably biology), as well as two A-Levels (or Highers). Mature students over the age of 21 may also gain entry by completing a college access course or demonstrating relevant work experience, such as employment as a health or nursing assistant. Currently, nursing education in the UK is structured as a three-year program that combines classroom-based coursework with practical placements in healthcare settings. The first year focuses on foundational knowledge, including anatomy, physiology, and basic healthcare skills. In the second year, students choose a specialization in one of four branches: adult nursing, pediatric nursing, mental health nursing, or learning disability nursing. Clinical placements during this time are tailored to the chosen specialty. For example, students specializing in pediatric nursing are assigned to pediatric units to develop skills specific to that field. In the third and final year, students complete their training, with the option to write degree-level essays or graduate with a diploma. Midwifery students follow a distinct pathway, specializing in midwifery from the beginning of their training. Upon graduation, all newly qualified nurses must register with the Nursing and Midwifery Council to practice legally and apply for jobs. United States The Yale School of Nursing, established in 1923, was the first autonomous nursing school in the United States. It operated independently with its own dean, faculty, budget, and degree program, adhering to university standards. Unlike earlier programs, its curriculum was based on an educational framework rather than the service needs of hospitals. In 1956, the Columbia University School of Nursing became the first institution in the U.S. to offer a master’s degree in a clinical nursing specialty. Prerequisites for nursing programs in the U.S. often include foundational courses in mathematics, English, and basic sciences. Advanced coursework in biology, anatomy, and physiology is also required. Core subjects include anatomy, physiology, pathology, and pharmacology. Additionally, there is a strong focus on procedural training, such as the insertion of intravenous and urinary catheters, sterile dressing changes, medication administration, and conducting physical examinations. After mastering basic skills in the first semester, students rotate through various clinical areas, including obstetrics, mental health, medical-surgical units, oncology, critical care, and pediatrics. This rotation provides a comprehensive understanding of the nursing profession. Many nursing schools and students utilize medical and healthcare educational software as a supplementary training tool. Upon completing their education, nursing students in the U.S. are eligible to take the national licensing examination to become either Licensed Practical Nurses (LPNs) or Registered Nurses (RNs). However, the rise of online nursing programs has significantly expanded access to nursing education. These innovative programs allow students to complete coursework remotely, enabling them to balance their studies with work, family, and community responsibilities. Online nursing programs create a virtual learning community, connecting students from across the country and providing a flexible pathway to earning a formal academic degree.
